title: Part Ten: Peter Thiel: the Mind

sections.brief: Thiel's texts read whole: 'The Straussian Moment' (2004 conference, 2007 volume pp. 189-218: Locke's X, Schmitt, Strauss, Girard, Echelon over the UN, preserve the katechon, side with peace); Cato 2009 sentences beyond the famous one (1920s, 'single person', 'politics is about interfering', follow-up rights list); Zero to One 2014 (creative monopoly vs 'illegal bullies or government favourites'); democracy in his own words 2016-2026 (NatCon 2019 speech, 2022 NatCon signature accepting the Constitution of 1787, Douthat 2025 'populism', Gellman pledge); ladder placement. Figures: time, compare

Girard's mimetic desire and scapegoat; Thiel's own words on meeting him; Imitatio 2007 (GSB; some say 2008); Girard vs Strauss in 2004; business use; Vance via the Yale talk (link de12); the katechon (2 Thess., Rome, Schmitt); Douthat 26 June 2025 exact quotes ('peace and safety', Thunberg, the hesitation, 'I obviously don't think that that's what I'm doing'); lectures SF Sept-Oct 2025 (Acts 17, off record, WaPo/Guardian audio, Farid), Paris 26 Jan 2026, Cambridge, Rome 15 Mar 2026; what the argument says and does not; labelled interpretation (palantiri, Girard inversion) with counter-reading. Figures: flow, time

Tensions, not contradictions, each with his own explanation: monopoly vs Palantir (2016 FASA suit won, $876M DCGS-A, US gov revenue $1.855bn FY2025); anti-democracy essay vs ~$32M 2022 (CNBC/FEC), 'populism still by far the best option', stagnation reason; privacy op-ed 2016 vs Palantir/Clearview, 'end indiscriminate surveillance', 'I obviously don't think...'; exit to NatCon signature; MIRI funding vs Yudkowsky as 'legionnaire'; worst-case reading tested. Figures: compare
